Our Curriculum Intent
Community and Kindness
All members of the school community will treat others with kindness and learn to value difference and celebrate diversity through acceptance and understanding.
Resilience and Independence
We will support learners to be self-motivated and ambitious, embracing each new day as an opportunity to succeed. We will develop resilience and help all children see struggle and mistakes as a natural part of becoming a more effective learner.
Creative and Critical Thinking
Our creative and engaging curriculum provides learners with the opportunities to question, analyse and problem solve. We encourage all children to set aspirational goals and work hard to reach them.

Latest News
What a brilliant first full week back at Foundry Lane! There has been so much lovely learning happening across the school. Year R have been busy settling into their new routines, exploring their learning environments and getting to know one another. Year 1 have been strengthening their hands ready for writing, while Year 2 have worked really hard on their Kinetic Letters handwriting and capital letters. Year 3 have started an exciting PE unit inspired by The Greatest Showman, Year 4 have been investigating which types of food packaging keep food freshest in DT, Year 5 have been talking about their reading preferences and preparing for Destination Reader, and Year 6 have begun their stomp dance unit, exploring different ways of moving their bodies to make sound. A huge thank you to all of our families for your patience, support and understanding during the power outage this week. We really appreciated everyone working with us while we managed an unexpected situation. Finally, please check your emails for the final vote for our new school house names! We are really excited to see which names our school community chooses. Have a lovely weekend, everyone!
What a lovely day welcoming our new Year R children to Foundry Lane! They enjoyed circle time, explored their new indoor and outdoor spaces and had a tour around the school. We were so proud to see them already beginning to follow our Golden Rules by being safe, being respectful and being their best. And a big well done to all the mums and dads too, who did brilliantly holding back those proud tears at the gate! A fantastic first day for everyone. Well done, Year R!
Early morning breakfast at Bolton's Bench - Civic award 2026
Our Year 6 children are all settled down for the night in their tents at Foxlease! This residential is an important part of their Civic Award – our own Junior Duke of Edinburgh-style programme , giving children the opportunity to develop resilience, independence, teamwork and confidence through new experiences. It's all part of our enrichment strategy, ensuring every child has the opportunity to Be Safe, Be Respectful and Be Their Best as they grow, challenge themselves and create memories that will last a lifetime.
What an exciting STEM day for our children! We were delighted to welcome David Hill from the University of Portsmouth, who worked with our children as they became engineers for the day! Using circuits and coding, they are designing, building, testing, evaluating and improving their own Smart Level-Crossing Safety Systems. We also welcomed Ben Aptor, who spoke to the children about railway safety in Southampton , helping them understand how to stay safe around railways while making meaningful real-world connections to their learning. A fantastic day of teamwork, problem-solving and inspiring future engineers!
Y4 are currently snuggled in their tents! They're being chatterboxes but are happy and laughing!
A huge thank you to the Lord Mayor for officially opening our wonderful new outdoor classroom today! We were delighted to welcome representatives from our Friends Committee, whose generous fundraising helped make this project possible , Andy, the talented artist who designed the space , our fantastic Steve , and our dedicated garden volunteers , all of whom have played an important part in bringing this vision to life. Our House Captains were also there to represent the pupils who will be enjoying the outdoor classroom regularly. They proudly showed the Lord Mayor around the garden, explaining how we use it and sharing their own experiences of learning in our new outdoor classroom. Finally, a heartfelt thank you to the Blackbird Environmental Fund for supporting this project. Together, you've helped us create a beautiful outdoor learning space where our children can learn, explore and thrive for many years to come.
A BIG well done to our Year 6 students this week who have faced their SATS with resilience & courage! We are so proud! Lots of smiles at our special breakfast this week and an inflatables and ice cream morning tomorrow!
A message we gave our Y6 pupils last night Mrs L x To our wonderful Year 6 pupils: Tomorrow is your chance to show just how far you've come Not just in scores, or spellings, or fractions and facts... but in resilience, kindness, courage and growth. You have learned through wobblers, laughed through mistakes, kept going when things felt tricky, and surprised yourselves time and time again. SATs do not measure your creativity, your humour, your kindness, your determination, or the way you make people feel. They are simply one small moment in your story. So tonight... take a deep breath, get a good sleep, and remember: You are ready. You are capable. And every single adult in school is already incredibly proud of you. Tomorrow, just do your best that has always been enough.
A HUGE well done to everyone from our community who took part in the Marathon festival over the weekend - especially those of you who were raising money for our Friends Committee! I had the pleasure of watching my sister at different points during the race and it was a brilliant atmosphere. An extra big well done to Marnie who did the 10k for Foundry Lane! If you'd like to sponsor our runners, here is the link: https://www.justgiving.com/campaign/friends-of-foundry-lane
Do you want to come and work for us?! We are looking for an excellent practitioner to join our wonderful team https://teaching-vacancies.service.gov.uk/jobs/teacher-d5c74f59-ccd8-438f-9dc2-8e66f506dda1
Well done to the runners in our friends committee! We will be cheering you on!
We've had a lovely first week back at school – it was so nice to see everyone's smiling faces at the gate each morning! It has also been lovely to see our new Year R list for next year! We are looking forward to welcoming current and new families into Year R! Year R became historians and went for a walk around the school, looking for objects that showed how the school has changed since it was founded in 1902 and how key moments in its history have been commemorated. Year 1 learnt about capacity in maths by using water and a range of different-sized containers. Year 2 have loved being creative and finishing off our art topic on flower heads . This week, we made flower heads using wax paper and coffee filters, decorating them with red, blue and yellow food colouring. We also created flower head sculptures from paper plates in the style of Yayoi Kusama, inspired by her love of polka dots . Year 3 enjoyed fantastic outdoor learning with Steve, building hazel fences using ancient weaving techniques as part of their art topic. Year 4 also went out with Steve to re-create the processes of the water cycle to conclude their Geography unit. Although they ended up a bit soggy, they had a great time! Year 5 have started their exciting history topic, Groundbreaking Greeks! They explored historical timelines, comparing the seven eras of Ancient Greece with what was happening in Britain and across the rest of the world at the same time. Year 6 have been working hard on their ski brochures , showing a real understanding of their audience and purpose, and carefully considering how to make them engaging and attractive to the reader. We hope you all have a lovely weekend!
Many many thanks to everyone at Foundry Lane for your kind words, hugs, cards and presents, as I said my goodbyes last week. I have had the BEST 24 years at Foundry Lane and that's down to the most wonderful children, their families, and the staff I have been lucky enough to work with. Foundry Lane is a special community that I will always cherish. Sending everyone kindness and love for the future. Mrs Phillips xx A Thank You from My Classroom Heart To the children... As I pack away my pens and books, And tidy up the shelves, I think of all the memories We've made here as ourselves. There's Beaky the Bird who joined our fun, Watching lessons come and go, And dance routines in church, Where our confidence would grow. Our school trips full of laughter, With adventure every day, And my love of penguins proudly shared In more lessons than I'll say! The pupil leaders group With their ideas great and true, Like Foundry Lane's Got Talent Where stars appearedlike you. We marched with smiles in the Rainbow Parade, Bright colours leading the way, Proving school can be a place Where we all shine every day. Now to staff... Thank you for helping me with tech issues, For our laughs, and dress up days For your love, care and compassion For lunch duties and wet plays! Because in every smile and helping hand, In every child we guide, This school is full of wonderful people Working side by side. And as we journey, wherever we go, Through every path in life we find, There's one small thing I stand for And that's the gift of being kind. Though new adventures wait ahead And different paths may start, Foundry Lane will always stay, A bright place in my heart.
Happy Easter to all our families celebrating today! We hope you have had a lovely day filled with joy, laughter and maybe a little chocolate too! Whether you have been spending time with family, heading out on an Easter egg hunt, attending church or simply enjoying a well-earned rest, we hope it has been a special one From all of us at school, Happy Easter!
It has been a wonderfully busy half term here at Foundry Lane! Year 4 have been making a splash with their swimming , while Year 5 have been busy making soup and learning all about where our food comes from . Year 1 enjoyed a fantastic trip to Tudor House , and our Year R children had a brilliant visit to the farm . Year 3 had a very exciting sleepover (or wake-over! ), and Year 2 have loved their paired reading sessions with Year 6 . Meanwhile, our Year 6 pupils have been exploring how humans have adapted and evolved over time . What a fantastic half term it has been! Wishing everyone who is celebrating over the Easter period a happy, restful and fun-filled time On Friday, we said our goodbyes to Mrs Phillips with a special shared assembly filled with singing , games and poetry . A huge thank you to Mrs DL for joining us during her parental leave and dressing up as the Easter Bunny – we can always rely on you to bring the fun! We wish Mrs Phillips every happiness in her new role as Headteacher of Chandlers Ford Infants . We know that Foundry Lane will always hold a special place in your heart, just as you will in ours
A wonderful Easter service that truly reflected the very best of our community spirit. Well done to our Year 3 and 4 pupils who performed so confidently, and to our Year 5 children for expertly managing the technical elementssuch a team effort. It was also a special moment as we said a fond farewell to Mrs Phillips, wishing her every success and happiness as she begins her exciting new journey into headship.
Eid Mubarak Wishing all of our families celebrating this evening and tomorrow a peaceful and joyful Eid. May this special time be filled with love, reflection and togetherness. From all of us at Foundry Lane, Eid Mubarak
Happy Mother's Day to all those who celebrate today. Today is a special opportunity to recognise the many wonderful women and caregivers who support, nurture and guide the children in our lives every day. We are incredibly grateful for everything you do. We also recognise that Mother's Day can be a difficult day for many people. Some may be remembering someone they love, missing family members, or finding today brings a mixture of emotions. At Foundry Lane, we want everyone in our community to know that you are seen, valued and appreciated, whatever today means for you. Wishing everyone in our school community a gentle and positive Sunday.
Such a wonderful day of bouncing! A BIG thank you to our friends committee for organising this. Friends of Foundry Lane Primary School
Thanks to all who came to our 'Wonderful Women's Breakfast' And an extra big thank you to our Year 6 helpers and Mrs Lush for supporting me run the event. I'd also like to extend my thanks to the friends committee for purchasing the pastries and to Mrs Maybe for purchasing all of the goodies for us! Mrs Loftus

Behaviour & Relational Practice
At Foundry Lane Primary School, we believe that positive relationships are the foundation of a successful school. Children learn best when they feel safe, valued, understood, and connected to the adults around them. Our relational approach underpins everything we do, creating a calm, consistent, and inclusive environment where every child can thrive.
Our practice is rooted in the understanding that behaviour is a form of communication. We seek to understand the reasons behind a child's behaviour, supporting them to develop the emotional regulation, resilience, and social skills they need to be successful learners and positive members of our school community. Our approach is relational and restorative, not punitive, and focuses on teaching, modelling, and reinforcing positive behaviour while providing appropriate support and clear boundaries.
All staff have received specialist training from our Educational Psychologist, ensuring a shared understanding of relational practice and the importance of responding to behaviour in a calm, consistent, and compassionate way.
Our dedicated Behaviour Manager works closely with staff, children, and families to ensure that support is timely, personalised, and effective. By identifying barriers early and working collaboratively with class teachers, leaders, and external professionals, we help children develop the strategies they need to succeed.
Every adult in school has a responsibility for building positive relationships with children, creating an environment where pupils feel a genuine sense of belonging.
Every school day at Foundry Lane begins with a personal welcome. Staff greet each child individually at the door, by name, giving every pupil a positive, calm start to their day and a moment of connection before learning begins. This small but important routine helps children feel noticed, valued, and ready to settle, and gives staff an early opportunity to notice how a child is feeling that morning, as well as teaching about consent.
Our three Golden Rules, Be Safe, Be Respectful, Be Your Best, are displayed in every classroom and explicitly taught throughout the year.
Rather than simply telling children what these rules mean, each class works together at the start of the year to co-create their own class charter, deciding as a group what Be Safe, Be Respectful, and Be Your Best actually look like in their classroom. This gives children a genuine say in shaping their own expectations, builds a real sense of ownership, and helps every child understand, in their own words, what it means to live our values day to day.
Children are taught that behaviour involves choices, and that every choice has a consequence. We use consistent, positive language to help children understand this, encouraging them to stay on the "green route," meeting our expectations and living our Golden Rules, and supporting them to return to it calmly and quickly if things go off track.
Our behaviour curriculum (co-created with the children) explicitly teaches pupils what Be Safe, Be Respectful, and Be Your Best look like in every part of school life, in the classroom, corridors, playground, toilets, canteen, and assembly. Expectations are clearly defined, consistently modelled by staff, and revisited regularly so that all pupils develop independence, self-regulation, and responsibility over time.
For example, being respectful in the canteen means using good manners and speaking in calm, quiet voices, while being your best in the playground means playing fairly, showing resilience, and being a positive role model for others. By teaching these expectations explicitly and consistently across every context, children build a clear, shared understanding of what our values look like in practice, wherever they are in school.
Positive behaviour is actively encouraged and celebrated through:
- Verbal and non-verbal praise
- Specific feedback linked to our Golden Rules
- Celebration in assemblies and classrooms
- Regular communication with parents and carers
- Whole-class reward systems, including Class Dojo
When difficulties arise, our focus is on repairing relationships rather than simply applying consequences.
Children are supported to:
- Reflect on their choices
- Understand the impact of their actions on others
- Take responsibility for their behaviour
- Rebuild relationships
- Develop strategies for making positive choices in the future
This restorative approach helps children develop empathy, accountability, and the confidence to resolve conflict respectfully. Where a consequence is needed, it is always proportionate, clearly linked to the behaviour, explained calmly, and focused on repair and learning, never used as a first response when a child is upset or overwhelmed.
We recognise that some children require additional support to regulate their emotions or overcome barriers to learning. Through our wider Thrive Provision, pastoral support, and targeted interventions, we ensure children receive the help they need while remaining fully included in school life wherever possible.
All children are encouraged to identify their "High-5" trusted adults in school, five people they know they can turn to with any worry or concern. Our relational approach sits alongside our attachment-aware practice and reflects our commitment to understanding each child's individual needs.
Strong relationships with families are central to our approach. We believe that children achieve the best outcomes when home and school work together with openness, honesty, and mutual respect.
Parents and carers are kept informed of both concerns and successes, involved early wherever additional support is needed, and treated with respect and openness at all times. We maintain regular communication with families through Arbor, phone calls, letters, and face-to-face meetings, and where a child is receiving additional behaviour support, parents receive regular updates on their progress.
By maintaining this ongoing communication and working collaboratively with parents and carers, we create consistent support for children both in school and at home.
Relational practice is not a standalone initiative: it is woven throughout every aspect of school life and underpins our behaviour culture.
Our Golden Rules, Be Safe, Be Respectful, Be Your Best, provide the foundation for the way we speak to one another, resolve difficulties, and celebrate success. Children are supported to understand that everyone makes mistakes and that, with the right support, everyone can learn, grow, and make positive choices.
At Foundry Lane, we believe that every child deserves to feel known, valued, and understood. By investing in positive relationships, maintaining high expectations, and responding with consistency and compassion, we create a culture where children feel safe to take risks, develop confidence, and achieve their full potential.
Through our relational approach, we are not simply managing behaviour: we are developing resilient, respectful, and emotionally literate young people who are ready to succeed both in school and beyond.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Foundry Lane Primary School
I warmly welcome you to Foundry Lane Primary School. I am very proud to be part of this vibrant, happy and caring school, where children are firmly at the heart of everything we do.
We are an inclusive school that values the contribution made by each child and their family, and we are proud of the cultural and linguistic diversity of our school community. Our school is a fantastic place to learn, play and work, with wonderful grounds and a real family feel, in the heart of Southampton.
Our curriculum is designed to be engaging and memorable, giving children the chance to ask questions, dig deeper, and take real pride in what they achieve. Alongside this, a wide range of enrichment opportunities, from trips and clubs to visitors and events, helps every child see what's possible for their future, whatever their starting point.
"Working Together" is more than a motto here; it shapes how our staff plan lessons, how we support each other, and how we involve families in every part of school life. We want every child to leave Foundry Lane with the confidence, character, and skills to play an active part in their community and in modern Britain.

English as an Additional Language
The children at Foundry Lane Primary School speak over 40 different languages in addition to English! Some of our staff speak different languages too.At Foundry Lane, we are proud of the rich linguistic diversity within our school community. We recognise that speaking more than one language is a real strength, and we are committed to making sure every child, whatever their starting point in English, is able to access our curriculum, make good progress, and feel a valued part of school life.
When a child for whom English is an additional language joins the school, this information is recorded so that we can build an accurate picture of their language needs. If a child is a New Arrival (defined as having been in the country for less than two months), their class teacher will carry out a new arrival assessment once the child has had time to begin settling in, usually around two weeks after starting.
This assessment looks at the child's proficiency in English and helps us understand what support they will need to access learning. Where appropriate, we work in partnership with families to gather information about the child's first language and educational background, so that we can plan effectively from the outset.
We track the progress of our EAL learners carefully, recognising that developing Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency (the more complex, subject-specific language needed to access the curriculum) takes time, even once a child appears confident in everyday spoken English.
It is important that EAL is not confused with a Special Educational Need. While some children may benefit from short, targeted withdrawal from class for specific interventions, this is kept to a minimum. Language acquisition is best supported through good, inclusive classroom strategies and thoughtful adaptation of the curriculum, rather than separation from peers. Children learn English most effectively when they have consistent access to strong language models around them, both from adults and from their classmates.
Sometimes we use the support of a Bilingual Assistant (BLA) from Southampton Language Service (SLS) who can work directly with children and families, using their first or home language to support access to the curriculum.
The service also provides access to World Stories, a collection of texts that children can read, or have read to them, in English or in a range of other languages, along with supporting activities and tracking tools. Southampton City Council is also a registered member of NALDIC, the leading national organisation supporting EAL practice, which gives our staff access to further specialist guidance and resources.
